extracted.intended_audience: writers, poets, artists, reviewers, and podcast readers considering submissions to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Official submission guidance for Strange Horizons magazine covering which departments accept work, where to find department-specific guidelines, confidentiality and copyright policies, and special notes (translated work, inclusivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Department-specific submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department of Strange Horizons has separate submission guidelines. For information about submitting work to a particular department, follow the appropriate link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments listed include: Art (how to submit art galleries and illustrations), Fiction (how to submit prose short stories), Non-Fiction (how to submit columns, essays, interviews, and round-tables), Poetry (how to submit literary, SF/F, slipstream, and speculative verse), Podcasts (how to audition as a podcast reader), Reviews (how to submit or request reviews of works of speculative and SF/F art and entertainment—especially books, films, games, and other similar media), Volunteering (how to join the Strange Horizons staff). Submitters should follow the guideline page specific to the department they are targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of submissions from marginalized and under-represented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: All of our departments encourage and welcome submissions by individuals from groups or backgrounds that have historically been marginalized and/or under-represented within Strange Horizons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit encouragement not to self-reject: 'Please don't self-reject; we want to consider your work!' This signals an editorial openness to diverse voices and an invitation to submit regardless of background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated fiction and poetry submission routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions of translated fiction or poetry can be made first to our sister magazine, Samovar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work is a translation, consider submitting to Samovar rather than directly to Strange Horizons (i.e., translated work has a preferred sister venue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions retention and confidentiality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to Strange Horizons may be retained in our archives for editorial reference, but are treated as confidential correspondence. We do not, however, guarantee absolute confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where material may be released: (1) If the magazine receives material containing explicit threats (they may share such material with legal authorities); (2) In an investigation of a specific incident of harassment or abuse initiated by a third party organization which specifically involves a work submitted to Strange Horizons or material present in communication with Strange Horizons, they may consider sharing a copy of that work or communication with the relevant organization; (3) They will comply with duly authorised subpoenas requesting material in their possession. The magazine will notify the author(s) involved if they share any of their work under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of work and categories accepted/published
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange Horizons is a weekly magazine of and about speculative fiction. We publish fiction, poetry, reviews, essays, interviews, and art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories and section labels used by the magazine include Art, Comics, Fiction, Reprint, Strange Lusts, Non-Fiction, 100African, Articles, Cartoons, Music, Azimuth, Azimuth Highlights, Editorials, Staff Stories, Columns, Reviews, Podcasts, Critical Friends, SH@25, Writing While Disabled, Poetry, etc. Use these categories to gauge fit and destination within the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and reproduction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All material in Strange Horizons is copyrighted to the original authors and may not be reproduced without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters and readers should assume that publication does not transfer reproduction rights and must obtain permission for reuse.
